full_judgment:
Mr. M. Enayetur Rahim, J: This Rule was issued calling upon opposite party to show cause as to why the order dated 20.05.2014 passed by the Special Judge, Noakhali in Special Case No.06 of 2013 arising out of G.R. No.81 of 2009 corresponding to Sudharam P.S. Case No.25 dated 29.01.2009 under Section 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and Section 109 'of the Penal Code rejecting the application filed by accused petitioners under Section 265(C) of the Cr. P.C. should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. One Shofiul Alam, Assistant Director of Anti-Corruption Commission of "Noakhali on 29.01.2009 lodged an FIR with the Sudharam Police Station alleging that present accused petitioners and the then Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali Shahadat Hossain Mojumdar and Shohidul Islam, former Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Noakhali and Md. Sahadat Hossain, former Executive Engineer, Public Works Department, Noakhali and Md. Benjamin Haider, former Senior Assistant Secretary, Housing and Works, Ministry of the Government of Bangladesh and Md. Mizanul Alam, former Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Nokhali collusively by misusing power and for their personal gain allotted 05 (five) acres land of different Moujas of Maijdee Twon among 383 applicants. Among whom 167 applicants were not businessmen. Present accused petitioner No.1 took allotment of 06 (six) plots in his name and also in the name of his 02(two) sons, sister-in-law and nephew and he also managed to recommended allotment of Chandina Bhiti to others including his personal men. Thus, accused persons committed offence under Section' 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act of 1947 and section 109 of the Penal Code. It was further alleged in FIR that the then Member of Parliament i.e. present accused-petitioner no.1 recommended the names of said 383 applicants traders for allotting plot in favour of them and Deputy Commissioner and Executive Engineer, Works Department, Noakhali and other accused persons in a meeting dated 20.12.2005 of 'Land Allotment Committee"  decided and recommended the names of 383 applicants and sent their names to Ministry of Housing and Works on 21.06.2006 and accused Benjamin Haider, former Senior Assistant Secretary of said Ministry approved the said list of 383 applicants and informed the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali vide letter dated 01.08.2006. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Admin), Noakhali sent the said list to Executive Engineer, Works Department, Noakhali i.e. accused Md. Shandat Hossain. The period of offence was in between 2005-2006. On the basis of the said FIR Sudharam P.S. Case No.25 dated 29.01.2009 under section 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act of 1947 and section 109 of the Penal Code was started which gave rise to G.R. No.81 of 2009. 

 4. The case being ready for trial the case record was transferred to the Senior Special Judge, Noakhali for trial and numbered as Special Case No.06 of 2013. 

 9. He further submits that accused petitioner No.1 was Member of Parliament till October, 2006 and as a Member of Parliament he recommended the prayer of affected shopkeepers to rehabilitate them in Noakhali town to carry their business as per Master Plan and such recommendation to the Ministry of Housing and Public Works did not disclose any offence and local officials prepared the final proposal and after scrutiny of the applications and necessary papers, they forwarded and recommended it to Ministry of Housing and ,Public Works which ordered for leasing out land to affected shopkeepers and accused petitioners were not signatory in orders for allotment of land to 383 applicants and accused petitioners were not the allotting authority and they had no involvement in the allotment process except recommendation as Member of Parliament and executive of association of affected shopkeepers. But, the learned Special Judge failed to consider these legal and factual aspects of the case is rejecting the applications for discharging the accused petitioners. 

 10. Mr. Khan referring to FIR, charge sheet and the documents annexed to the application lastly submits that no offence has been disclosed within the mischief of section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with section 109 of the Penal Code. As such, the order of framing charge against the accused petitioners is illegal and liable to set aside. 

 11. However, Mr. J.K. Paul, the learned Advocate, appearing for the opposite party no.2 Anti-Corruption Commission, has opposed the Rule and submits that the Anti-Corruption Commission after holding proper investigation having found prima facie case against the petitioners submitted charge sheet and the submission made by the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners are misconceived and as such there is no scope to quash the proceedings at this stage. 

 14. Criminal misconduct has been defined in section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 which runs as follows; Criminal Misconduct—(1) A public servant is said to commit the offence of criminal misconduct- 

 15. From the FIR and charge sheet it appears that intotal 496.75 acres of land in Maijdee twon was acquired by the Government for the then C.B. Department vide LA Case No.02/1920-21, 20/1963-1962, 15/1966-67 and 24/1966-67. Eventually, the affected businessman by rever erosion started various business in the different areas of Maijdee town illegally occupying Government Land. But at one stage, they were evicted by local administration and Government decided to rehabilitate the affected persons, and in the year 1972 and 1982 two lists were prepared mentioning 835 persons as illegal occupants. But they made demand that they might be recognized as affected businessman. In the year 1996, Ministry of Works approved a master plan for Noakhali town and recommend to rehabilitate said 835 affected businessman as per the master plan. However, in between 1999-2003 some of the affected businessman started businessmen in the Government land taking 'one year' lease from the Executive Engineer, PWD, Noakhali. But in the year 2003 Ministry of Works directed to cancel said one year lease and to take necessary steps for rehabilitate 835 affected businessmen. Against the said decision 56 writ petitions were filed before the High Court Division and order of injunction was also passed in those writ petitions. Eventually, the Rules were made absolute and High Court Division directed to deliver possession of respective land, which were leased out to the respective petitioners within a period of 30(thirty) days on receipt of the said order. In such a situation, the local people, businessmen, local Member of Parliament, petitioner No.1, local Administration jointly took initiative to resolve the issue and on 27.08.2005 in a meeting of নোয়াখালী জেলা উন্নয়ন ও সমন্বয় কমিটি presided by over Mr. Moudud Ahmed, the then, Minister of Law and Justice, it was decided that as per master plan of Noakhali town a complex in the name and style "Prottasha Biponi Bitan" would be constructed for rehabilitation of the affected businessman and District Land Allotment Committee would take necessary decision for preparing the list of affected businessman and the list was to be sent to the Ministry of Publik Works for its approval. And accordingly Executive Engineer, Publik Works, Noakhali invited application from the affected businessman and ultimately "District Land Allotment Committee" in its meeting dated 20.12.2005 prepared a list of 383 affected persons and after recommending the said list sent the same to the Ministry of Public Works and then Ministry approved the said list. After approval of the said list Executive Engineer, Publik Works, Noakhali executed lease deed in favour of the respective allottees taking consideration money fixed by the Government. Allegation has been made against the accused petitioners that they had made recommendation to said 383 applicants for allotting land/shops and some of their family members and relatives were also get allotment. 

 17. It is now well settled that mere recommendation is not enough to constitute an offence within the mischief of section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. In the case of Moudud Ahmed V. State reorted in 11 BLC, page-430 it has been held that mere recommendation is not an offence, the authority who acts on the basis of the recommendation is to scrutinize of the legality and validity of the recommendation before implementation of the recommendation. Recommendation for a thing on of a person is not binding upon the implementation authority." 

 18. It appears from the record that proceedings in respect of accused Md. Shandat Hossian, former Executive Engineer, Public Works Department, Md. Sahadat Hossain Mojumder, the then Deputy Commission and Chairman 'Land Allotment Committee' has ben quashed vide Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.33084 of 2010 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.30912 of 2012 respectively and other officials who were involved with the allotment process were discharged from the case. And having regard to the fact that the Anti-Corruption did not take away step against the order of quashement before the Appellate Division as well as the order of discharge. It also appears from annexure F to the application that High Court Division in writ petition No.3446 of 2007 had endorsed the list of said 383 applicants. Thus, if we all to continue of the present proceeding against the present petitioners only, without prosecuting the principle accused, the Government officials who were involved with the allotment process under Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with section 109 of the Penal Code, it will be nothing but abuse of the process of the Court. 

 20. Having considered and discussed as above, we are of the view that the learned Special Judge without considering the leagal aspect with the facts and circumstances of the present case passed the impugned order rejecting the prayer for discharging the accused petitioners and thereby, erred in law. And thus, same is liable to be set aside. 

 21. The order dated 20.05.2014 passed by the Special Judge of Special Tribunal, Noakhali rejecting the application filed by accused petitioners under section 265(C) of the Cr. P.C. in Special Case No.06 of 2013 arising out of G.R. No.81 of 2009 of the corresponding to Sudharam P.S. Case No.28 dated 29.01.2009 under section 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and section 109 of the Penal Code is hereby set aside.
